correctness.rationale: For fixed support S of two-label defenders, pointwise-minimal Roman f is uniquely canonical: two on S, zero on outside neighbors of S, ones on undominated vertices. Each two needs a private zero neighbor dominated by no other two; otherwise a one-step downward change remains feasible. In G∨H, partition S as empty (one all-ones term), one shore only (old minimal RDFs plus singleton isolated defenders in that shore), or both shores (exactly one nonuniversal defender in each shore, every remaining vertex zero). The cases are disjoint, giving R_join=R_G+R_H-z^n-z^m+z^(n+m)+i(G)s z^(n+1)+i(H)s z^(m+1)+p(G)p(H)s² z^4, with K1 convention p(K1)=0 and i(K1)=1. Independent exhaustive enumeration of every graph on each shore for sizes one to three (121 graph pairs) and every 3-labeling directly tested feasibility and all coordinate decreases, matching every bivariate coefficient. Infinite graph identity is from support proof, not finite checks; union multiplication and join recurrence give coefficient computation on cotrees.
residual_risks: Pointwise minimality is not minimum weight; all feasible Roman domination polynomial is different.

value.rationale: Complete two-variable composition law for arbitrary nonempty graph joins converts pointwise-minimal Roman enumeration into factor polynomials and simple isolate/nonuniversal counts, including exact mixed-defender correction. With disjoint-union multiplication it supplies an exact polynomial cotree recurrence for cographs, a naturally motivated counting gain beyond Roman domination numbers.
residual_risks: Computing factor enumerators on unrestricted graphs can be expensive; no claim of efficient general graph counting.

limitations: All nonempty simple graph joins, including K1 and disconnected; pointwise minimal only, not general feasible/minimum-weight census.
